status_summary: No move of the Real Estate Assessment Center to the Office of Housing was found; a HUD notice published 2026-09-29 (91 FR 61432) on NSPIRE scoring, issued jointly by the Housing and Public and Indian Housing offices, lists the center within Public and Indian Housing. A HUD Inspector General report of 2026-08-31 describes the center as now named the Assessment, Recovery and Oversight Center, coordinating inspection procurement for Public Housing and Multifamily Housing properties, with its management response issued on a Public and Indian Housing memorandum. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, Public Law 119-101, enacted 2026-07-11, lets inspections under LIHTC, HOME and certain rural housing programs satisfy initial Housing Choice Voucher inspections and directs HUD and USDA to explore joint physical inspections, according to a CRS report; these streamline inspections across programs but do not provide private accreditation.

timeline.event: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (P.L. 119-101) became law without signature; section 405 lets LIHTC, HOME and certain rural housing inspections satisfy initial voucher inspections, and section 802 directs HUD and USDA to explore joint physical inspections.

title: Move HUD REAC to the Office of Housing and allow private accreditation of inspections
uncertainties: The NSPIRE scoring notice (91 FR 61432) was read in full on the Federal Register host and lists the Real Estate Assessment Center within the Office of Public and Indian Housing, with no mention of a rename, reorganization or private accreditation; it is cited as status evidence, not as a step. The HUD Inspector General report 2026-CH-0003 of 2026-08-31 was read on oversight.gov and gives the new name but no date for the rename and no move to the Office of Housing; no Federal Register document on the rename was found. The govinfo.gov text of Public Law 119-101 confirmed its enactment date and the titles of sections 405 and 802 in the table of contents, but the web version was cut off before those sections, so their content rests on the CRS report. The alternative inspections information collection of 2025 was seen in a listing but not read.
